$comment: Pins Go and TypeScript to one verdict on HDF documents carrying a wrongly-typed field. Go decodes into generated structs, so encoding/json rejects these outright; TypeScript parsed untyped and cast, and `as T` is erased at runtime, so the same bytes converted and the bad value reached the output — as a wrong title, a silently zeroed impact, or a dropped reference. Every document here is invalid HDF; the question the table settles is what a converter does with input the schema rejects. Both languages now validate at the shared guard, so both reject. Cases are a base document plus one mutation, because the mutation is the whole point of the case.

cases.name: title as a number
cases.why: TypeScript wrote 42 into the CSV Title column

cases.name: impact as a string
cases.why: the dangerous member: TypeScript emitted impact 0.00 while severity still read medium — a wrong number in a compliance report, not an obviously broken cell

cases.name: refs as a non-array
cases.why: TypeScript dropped the reference and emitted an empty References cell

cases.name: cwe as a non-array
cases.why: the member hdf-to-csv patched locally in .23 because a mixed array made TypeScript invent 'CWE-79; 2; '

cases.name: cwe array with a non-string entry
cases.why: the mixed array that made hdf-to-csv invent 'CWE-79; 2; '; it is why .23 added a local cweCell patch, which this guard replaces
